name: Garaiko artea (the Encina de Garai / Encina de Etxeita)
age_estimate: documented only as "centenaria" (very old); no numeric age given by any source

location.address: In the meadow of the Etxeita farmhouse, opposite the Santa Kataliñe/Santa Catalina hermitage, off the BI-3341 road between Goiuria (Iurreta) and Garai, Garai, Bizkaia
location.neighbourhood: Etxeita caserio grounds, Garai (Durangaldea district), Bizkaia

access: Free but on working farmland: from the Santa Catalina/Santa Kataliñe hermitage on the BI-3341 between Goiuria and Garai, a paved track crosses about 800m of pine wood to the Etxeita farmhouse; the tree stands in the meadow just north of the farm buildings. The official Bizkaia government listing notes an information panel stands at the tree, and a Basque tourism site (MugaKultura, Oct 2025) gives these exact directions and actively invites visitors, while asking them to respect the place and the people who live there. Flagging for a future access check (e.g. OSM path tags) rather than treating the farmhouse setting as settled.
transport: Rural Durangaldea, Bizkaia; no public transport reaches the farm track. Garai and neighbouring Iurreta are about 26km from Bilbao (which we already publish); a car is the realistic way to reach it.
verify_notes:
THREE SOURCES, well past the two-source bar: (1) bizkaia.eus, the Diputacion Foral de Bizkaia's own official monumental-tree register page, listing this as Natural Monument 'Encina de Garai (ES213002)', species 'Quercus ilex ilex', with coordinates Lat 43.19801828 / Long -2.62562536 (matches this lead's coordinate, 43.197819/-2.625761, to within a few metres, so location_precision is confirmed on the register's own tree-level coordinate); (2) es.wikipedia.org's 'Arboles singulares de la Comunidad Autonoma del Pais Vasco' article, an independent encyclopedia entry with its own description and citations; (3) mugakultura.eus, a Basque local-culture/tourism site's article dated 2025-10-23 (fetched and read directly, not taken from a search summary), marking the tree's 30th anniversary of protection and confirming it is still standing and actively promoted as a place to visit AS OF LATE 2025, which is good recent alive-evidence.

DESIGNATION: protected since 1995 under Decreto 265/1995 (Gobierno Vasco), one of the Basque Country's first legally protected singular trees; it automatically became a legal 'monumento natural' under later Basque conservation law per the bizkaia.eus page's own text.

DIMENSIONS: the bizkaia.eus register gives an actual TRUNK figure, not a search-summary guess: 5.7m perimeter measured at 1.3m height (girth_cm 570 above is this measured figure, not derived), stem/bole height 0.8m, total height 8.5m, crown diameter 20m. Wikipedia and MugaKultura both separately describe the CROWN (not the trunk) as having a circumference of 'more than 60 metres' and a diameter of 'more than 19 metres', consistent with the register's 20m crown-diameter figure; do not let the writer confuse the ~60m CROWN circumference with the tree's actual 5.7m TRUNK girth, they describe different things.

AGE: no source anywhere gives a number. Wikipedia's generic list labels it 'Centenario' (i.e. very old, unspecified) and MugaKultura calls it 'esta encina centenaria'; both are vague and I kept them vague per the rule rather than inventing a figure. Recorded age_min/age_max as null (empty) rather than guessing from girth, because I have no published Quercus ilex growth-rate figure to derive from and the sources themselves decline to give a number; a reader with local knowledge or a dendrologist could answer this on the page.

STORY MATERIAL: shaped by generations of pruning to feed livestock on its acorns, which gave it the wide symmetrical crown; oral tradition says a flock of up to 360 sheep has sheltered under it. Views over the Durangaldea mountains from the meadow.

ACCESS, the genuinely open question: the tree stands on the grounds of a still-working, apparently inhabited farmhouse (Etxeita). This is NOT a doorbell-and-permission case (no source describes needing to ask anyone, there is a marked track and an official information panel, and a tourism site actively gives turn-by-turn directions and encourages the visit), but it is also not an unambiguous public park either, and the tourism piece explicitly asks visitors to be respectful of the people living there. I am delivering this per 'publish what verifies, the access call gets an honest caveat rather than a hold', flagging it so a later pass can settle it further with an OSM foot/access tag check on the BI-3341-to-Etxeita track (the Ypres technique), which I did not have time for in this pass.

DESTINATION CALL: an individually named, 30-year-designated holm oak with a real local story (the 360 sheep, the pastoral pruning, an information panel, an active 2025 tourism write-up), but modest in absolute size (8.5m tall) and, like Eraulgo artea, sitting alone in farmland rather than in any existing cluster: 26.1km from Bilbao (published), 71km from Eraulgo artea, 28.6km from Ondategiko Haritza (the closest of the four to it, but still outside a walkable or day-trip radius), 110.8km from Roble Escarcio. Recording the verified facts; the container decision (single-famous-tree exception, a future Durangaldea/Garai cluster, or staying a lead) is not mine to force.

CURATOR CALL, 2026-09-27: Recommend HOLD. No numeric age (only 'centenaria'), and the tree stands in a working farmhouse's meadow reached by an 800m track through someone's land; the tourism writeup invites visitors but this is thinner ground than the other four trees in this batch, which all carry either a real age figure or an unambiguous public access statement. Kept as a lead rather than a standalone place; would sit well in a future Durangaldea/Bizkaia cluster if other trees turn up nearby.

name: Ondategiko Haritza (the Roble de Ondategi / Roble de Sarragoa)
age_estimate: documented only as "centenario" (very old); no numeric age given by any source

location.address: On the campa (communal meadow) of Sarragoa, at the southwest edge of Ondategi, at the end of the street to the left of the church, Zigoitia, Alava/Araba
location.neighbourhood: Ondategi, a small village of Zigoitia municipality, Alava/Araba

access: Free. Stands on an open communal meadow (campa) at the village edge, reached by the street that runs left of the church; no gate, ticket or private-land caveat found in any source. Also known locally as the Roble de Sarragoa / Sarragoako haritza / Arbol gordo de Zanagua.
transport: Rural Zigoitia, Alava; no realistic public transport. About 13km from Vitoria-Gasteiz (unpublished) and 38km from Bilbao (published); a car is the realistic way to reach it.
verify_notes:
THREE INDEPENDENT SOURCES: (1) es.wikipedia.org's 'Arboles singulares de la Comunidad Autonoma del Pais Vasco' article, giving species, height and the festival history, citing the official Basque Government declaration; (2) euskal-herria.org/node/24472 (a 2011 post by a hiking/nature site contributor named Inaxio), independently confirming species, height 20m, ~30m spread, condition 'Ona' (good), and the alternate name Sarragoako haritza, and itself citing the old Eusko Jaurlaritza biodiversity database (a dead link today, http://www1.euskadi.net/biodiversidad/fichaarbol.apl, 404 and not in the Wayback Machine, so not counted as a live source, but the citation shows the underlying government designation existed at that URL); (3) paisajesdealava.blogspot.com (fetched directly, not from a search summary), which cites 'Gobierno Vasco - Eusko Jaurlaritza - Declaracion de arboles Singulares' explicitly as its source and gives the same measurements as the WebSearch AI summary, CONFIRMING those figures actually appear on a real page rather than being a search-tool invention: perimeter at 1.3m = 4.9m, bole height 2m, total height 20m, crown diameter 30m. Species, dimensions and the pre-Civil-War San Lorenzo romeria story are consistent across all three.

DESIGNATION: Singular Tree of the Basque Country since 1997, one of Alava's ten protected singular trees per the same sources; separately noted (WebSearch summary only, not independently fetched, so treated as a lead not a fact) that it featured on an ONCE lottery ticket in the 'Abraza tu arbol' series.

GIRTH: girth_cm above (490) is the register's own measured trunk PERIMETER at 1.3m, not a derived figure.

AGE: no source gives a number, only 'centenario' (an old tree, unspecified), kept vague per the rule. age_min/max left null rather than derived: I have no cited Quercus robur growth-rate figure to derive from, and inventing one from the 490cm girth alone would be exactly the kind of guess this project forbids.

LOCATION: I could not find an official government coordinate fetched directly (unlike the Navarra and Bizkaia trees in this same batch, where the register itself gave a lat/lon); a Geocaching cache page for this tree exists (GC4EC9X) but hides its exact coordinate behind a login wall, so I could not use it. This lead's own coordinate (42.95363042, -2.73524306) is consistent with Ondategi village's known location, and the sources agree the tree stands at the SOUTHWEST EDGE of the village on the Sarragoa meadow, next to the street left of the church, which is village-level/street-level knowledge rather than a surveyed tree point. Marking location_precision 'approximate' honestly rather than upgrading it on no real evidence.

STORY MATERIAL: for generations gave shade and shelter to livestock and people at village festivals; until the Spanish Civil War the village held its San Lorenzo romeria (10 August) under its crown, with a lone accordion player providing music because the village could only afford paid musicians for the Santa Lucia festival (13 December). A good, specific, sourced anecdote.

ACCESS: a communal village meadow at a street's end, no restriction found anywhere; this is the most straightforwardly open-access tree of the four in this batch.

DESTINATION CALL: individually named, government-designated since 1997, with a genuine, specific historical anecdote (the pre-war romeria) that the other three trees in this batch lack. Still modest in scale next to Spain's true giants, and geographically isolated from any published place: 13.0km from Vitoria-Gasteiz (unpublished, and even that is beyond an easy walk), 38km from Bilbao (published), 28.6km from Garaiko artea (the nearest of this batch), 61.8km from Eraulgo artea, 83.1km from Roble Escarcio. Recording the verified facts; the container decision is not mine to force, though of the four in this batch this is the one I would flag as having the strongest standalone story.

CURATOR CALL, 2026-09-27: Recommend HOLD. No numeric age (only 'centenario') and location_precision is approximate rather than confirmed (village-edge description, no surveyed coordinate). A fine local oak but the destination test ('would somebody travel specifically for this one tree') does not clear on fame or scale alone without a real age or measured pin. Kept as a lead.

name: Olmo centenario de Millena (Om centenari de Millena)

location.address: Plaza de la Iglesia de Sant Josep, Millena, El Comtat, Alicante province, Comunitat Valenciana
location.neighbourhood: Church square (Plaza de la Iglesia), village centre of Millena

access: Free. Stands in the open church square (Plaza de la Iglesia de Sant Josep) in the centre of the small village of Millena (population around 200); lacantimploraverde.es describes it as easy to find, with the village itself putting up signage pointing visitors to it at the entrance to town.
transport: Rural inland Alicante province (El Comtat comarca), between Gorga and Cocentaina; no public transport reaches the village. Roughly 65km from Alicante city (published) and well outside any day-trip boundary from it; realistically reached by car, e.g. from Cocentaina or Alcoi (neither currently published).
verify_notes:
THREE SOURCES fetched directly (none from search-summary figures alone): (1) lacantimploraverde.es (2015), a travel blog with its own visit and photos, giving the plaza location, the local legend that it is popularly called 'Olmo milenario' (thousand-year elm) though the blogger's own theory ties planting to the 1812 Cadiz Constitution ('La Pepa', elms were symbolically planted across Spanish towns then) for an age of ~203 years -- this specific '1812 planting' theory is the AUTHOR'S OWN SPECULATION, not a documented planting record for this specimen, so I am not treating it as a derived age (it is exactly the kind of bridge claim BRIEF_RESEARCH.md warns about: a general planting custom joined to one unconfirmed tree). The same source states explicitly the tree is NOT on the official Catalogo de arboles monumentales y singulares de la Comunitat Valenciana, but is generically protected under Ley 4/2006 de Patrimonio Arboreo Monumental de la Comunidad Valenciana, and calls it 'the last plaza elm in good health in Alicante province', with support pillars added after a snow-laden branch broke. (2) practicomagazine.com (2016), an independent regional-tourism magazine piece on Millena, giving diameter 5m and height 10m and calling it 'tricentenario' (three-hundred-year-old), confirming the plaza location. (3) geocaching.com's own cache page for 'Om mil.lenari / Olmo milenario' at this site, giving height 10m, trunk circumference 5.30m, crown diameter up to 11m, repeating the 300+ years estimate, the same 'last healthy plaza elm in the province' claim, the same Ley 4/2006 protection and the same Dutch-elm-disease (grafiosis) context. Three independent sources agree closely on the dimensions (girth ~530cm) and on the vague '300 years' figure, so age_estimate is kept as the sources' own vague repeated figure ('roughly 300 years', banded 200-300) rather than sharpened, and the 1812-planting theory is left out of age_min/max entirely, recorded here only as colour for the writer.

GIRTH: recorded girth_cm as 530 (the geocache page's 5.30m trunk circumference), corroborated by practicomagazine's 5m diameter figure (5m diameter implies ~1571cm circumference via pi, which does NOT match 530cm circumference -- practicomagazine's 'diametro' figure looks like a loose/incorrect use of the word, most likely meaning crown spread or a misstatement, since 530cm circumference implies a trunk diameter of only ~169cm; flagging this unit/word confusion rather than silently picking one).

SPECIES: Ulmus minor (field elm/common elm), consistent across all three sources and with the Commons category name ('om' is Catalan/Valencian for elm); no source gives finer taxonomic detail, in line with the usual local-name-only situation.

ALIVE: all three sources describe an actively maintained, currently standing tree (support pillars added and later one pillar itself damaged by a subsequent snowfall, per the geocache page), and three Commons photographs by a known Catalan tree photographer (Joanbanjo) are dated 2013-06-02, showing roots, bark and branches in apparently healthy condition. No death, felling or decline report found in any search. However nothing found is dated later than 2016, so recency is thinner than ideal; flagging on that basis per the bar (confirmation thin rather than absent) rather than holding the tree back.

LOCATION: the lead's coordinate (38.730569, -0.363691) is NOT a tree-level fix -- none of the three 2013 Commons photos of this tree carry a geotag (checked directly via the Commons API), and this exact coordinate matches to five decimal places the OSM administrative-boundary CENTROID for the village of Millena as a whole (Nominatim: 38.7305669, -0.3638185), i.e. it is a village-level point that happens to sit close to the plaza because Millena is a very small, compact village (~215 residents). An Overpass query for the village's own church (Esglesia de Sant Josep de Millena, way 753200043) returns 38.7307031, -0.3635072, about 22m from the lead coordinate and consistent with all sources placing the tree in that church's own square. Marking location_precision 'approximate': we know the plaza with confidence (in front of the Church of Sant Josep, centre of Millena) but not a tree-level pin, and the given coordinate should be read as 'the village/plaza area', not 'the trunk'.

DESTINATION CALL: a real, checkable curiosity (explicitly the last healthy plaza elm surviving Dutch elm disease in the whole of Alicante province, per two independent sources) with genuine size for the species (530cm girth, comparable to Navajas's verified 630-650cm elm) and a visible, photographable detail (the support pillars holding up its heavy limbs). It has no national Tree-of-the-Year title or Wikidata item of its own (checked, none found), so it is a notch below Navajas's or Aprisquillo's documentation. It sits about 65km from Alicante (published) with no transit link, well outside any day-trip boundary, and there is no other published or nearby-verified tree to cluster it with, so it stands alone or waits as a well-documented lead; recording the verified facts either way per 'publish what verifies, the container decision is not mine to force'.

CURATOR CALL, 2026-09-27: Recommend HOLD. Not on any official monumental-tree register (unlike the five trees shipped from this same batch), location_precision is approximate (the lead's coordinate is the village's OSM administrative centroid, not a tree-level fix; no geotagged photo found), and it sits 65km from Alicante with no realistic day-trip transit. A real age (roughly 300 years) and a real story (last healthy plaza elm to survive Dutch elm disease in the province) keep it worth revisiting if a sharper pin or a register entry ever turns up. Kept as a lead.
